note: Figures for the OCOKA lens of the Ground Guide. Per-weapon ranges live in Symbols.json (the `Rng` field of each entry); this file holds everything that is not one symbol's own figure. Every figure has a basis: D = read from a pamphlet in Material/ (cited), C = from the existing catalogue (WeaponEqptV3.json), T = typical public figure (mine, to confirm), E = my estimate or proposal (to confirm). The planner corrects the T and E figures; they are not doctrine.
handling: The D figures are numbers read from Pakistan Army pamphlets (IC, IBB). Keep this file under the same handling terms as those pamphlets before it goes outside the owner's own systems.

visibilityRules.note: Doctrine says rain, dust, mist, haze and fog reduce the effectiveness of night vision devices (IBB p201) but gives no figures; the caps below are my proposal. The grid is NOAA GSOD, 2016-2025, 174 stations, on the climate grid (5 arc-minutes); read it as what the nearest airport sees. GSOD gives a DAILY MEAN view, so it understates short fog episodes; haze is a proxy (a view of 3 km or less on a day with no fog, rain, snow, hail or thunder flag, so it also catches dust and smoke). An ordinary day on the plains has a mean view of 4-5 km, which is why the proxy uses 3 km, not 5.

layers: vis_mean_NN: mean view, 0.1 km, capped at 16 km
lt2km_NN: % of days with a view under 2 km
fog_NN: % of days with the fog flag
dist: km to the nearest usable station
grid.trust: dist over 100 km: say so on the card; Gilgit-Baltistan and the far south-west of Balochistan are 150 km or more from a usable station (Skardu 153 km, Gilgit 187 km)

visibilityRules.rangeLimit: visual detection range = min(device range, meteorological visibility)

nvdCap.thermal: no cap in haze or dust; 0.5 x view on a fog day
nvdCap.note: On an ordinary 4-5 km day the cap does not bite (devices reach 0.3-1 km); it does in fog and thick haze. Example: fog day, view 0.5 km, image intensifier cut to about 250 m.

visibilityRules.cardWording: In <month> at <place>: fog on N % of days, view 3 km or less on M %, mean view X km; the nearest station is D km away.

rules.rule: The frontage of a company, platoon or section cannot be extended; a battalion's frontage grows by widening the gaps.
Platoon and section frontages must stay within what a commander controls by word of mouth. Gaps are covered by fire, minefields and link patrols.
In built-up areas a platoon's frontage should never exceed 100 m, ideally one house.

rules.rule: The enemy's amphibious, fording and bridging means have reduced the obstacle value of canals. Brick-lined canals with water 1-1.5 m below the bank still trouble tanks; banks as deep as 6-9 m may have to be cut.
An enemy minefield on a water obstacle is generally 600-900 m deep.
Protective minefields are laid close to the forward defended localities and covered by fire, normally up to 250-300 m deep.

reverseSlope.limits: hard to keep observation; direct-fire range is short; obstacles on the forward slope cannot be covered by direct fire; guard against being seen from a distant feature or the flank

surfaceBlockers.note: What stands in a line of sight that a 30 m elevation model cannot show. aboveDsmM = its height above the model (the model already holds part of a canopy or a roof line); share = the chance that a line through one patch of it is blocked; ownShare = the chance that a man standing in it is hidden by it (the same as share when not given); grainM = the size of one patch of it (a field, a clump), so that a line crossing several cells of one patch counts it once. The lens works out the CHANCE that a line is clear: nothing is random and nothing is certain, so the cards say 'may be seen' and 'check on the ground'. Buildings use the bundle's building layer instead of a class (built). Tall crops use cropCalendar.

built.note: By the building layer's classes (rules.json grotbc.layers.bld). A line of length L through buildings scattered at density n, each w wide, meets one with chance 1 - exp(-n w L).
built.heightNote: height classes: not known or under 3 m, 3-6 m, 6-12 m, 12 m and over; about half the building height is taken to stand above the 30 m model

cropCalendar.note: PROPOSAL, from general knowledge of the crops of the irrigated plains; to be replaced by a published crop calendar (FAO GIEWS country calendar, Sacks et al. 2010) or the owner's own. tall = tall enough to hide a standing man (about 1.5 m or more); hides = hides a crouching or prone man (about 0.8 m or more). threatAxis.note: Where the enemy is: an option the planner repositions on the map, not read from enemy symbols (user, 2026-11-10). By default the threat comes from the front.

modes.front: the threat bearing is the unit's front: groundGuide.footprint.bearingDeg (0 = north today), so the frontage and the threat agree
modes.fixed: a bearing set by dragging the handle on the map (stored apart from the footprint facing)
modes.allRound: all-round: judge every direction and report the worst, as the footprint's worst-of-4 / circle modes do

threatAxis.handle: a draggable arrow on the map at the symbol or at the area's centre; dragging its tip turns the bearing, dragging its body moves the origin; follows the symbol unless it has been moved
threatAxis.persist: with the plan, like the Gr Scope target
threatAxis.keepsToGrotbc: the GROTBC verdict and enforce mode do not read the threat axis

policy.wording: Say 'may be seen from' and 'check on the ground', never 'hidden' or 'safe', from elevation alone (30 m cells show tree tops and roofs, not 1-2 m bunds).
policy.enforce: Enforce mode stays on the GROTBC GO / NO-GO rule in the OCOKA lens. An OCOKA verdict is a judgement call and never blocks a placement.
policy.keys: GROTBC keeps its keys (G R O T B C K D S P H V and Esc). OCOKA uses others.
